_comment: v3 config for Stanford MyChart. Validated end-to-end against the live portal on 2026-06-06 — 142 visits + 106 notes with content scraped. Stanford uses the same Epic MyChart API surface as UCSF (same instance number, same endpoint paths, same response shapes), differing only in base_path (Stanford uses /myhealth_sso, UCSF uses /UCSFMyChart). The branded patient-facing site at myhealth.stanfordhealthcare.org embeds Epic in a cross-origin iframe; the actual Epic MyChart lives at mychart.stanfordhealthcare.org/myhealth_sso/. After SSO from the wrapper, mychart.* cookies are set; navigating directly to mychart.stanfordhealthcare.org/myhealth_sso/Visits gives the runtime full access — but Stanford sets `body { display: none }` as a frame-busting protection, which the runtime must override (CSS override at runtime) before any UI it injects (e.g., the save button) is visible.
name: Stanford MyHealth (via Epic MyChart)

auth._keepalive_comment: Stanford has independent session timers per origin: the wrapper at myhealth.* and the API host at mychart.* each idle-time-out on their own. Long scrapes (~100 visits at ~10s each = ~17 min) outrun the default ~10-15 min timeout, so we ping both. Image-GET tactic = no CORS preflight; browser carries cookies.

upcoming_visits._comment: Upcoming visits live in a different Epic component than past visits. At Stanford it's instance 5 (the UpcomingVisits component) which doesn't expose RenderedData; its work-list is in Data.NextNDaysVisits + Data.LaterVisitsList + Data.InProgressVisits. Each entry has Csn, Instant, PrimaryDate, VisitTypeName, PrimaryDepartment, PrimaryProvider, Organization, etc. — enough to build a planned Encounter without any additional API call. (IsClinicalInformationAvailable is false on upcoming visits, so there's nothing to fetch.) The convert_to_v2_bundle.py converter handles this shape via its `--upcoming` mode and emits status='planned' Encounters.
upcoming_visits._no_endpoint: This job has no endpoint — the RD-equivalent entry from discovery IS the full payload. The runtime currently still calls an endpoint per item; until that supports a no-call mode, this job is run as a save-the-discovered-list-to-file flow rather than via runner.run().
